settings.headline:
Wood, worked by hand,
for the long haul.
settings.copy: Hearth & Grain is a working wood shop where solid oak and honest joinery meet a lifetime guarantee. We build custom furniture, bring heirloom pieces back to life, and teach the craft at the bench — one board, one joint, one piece at a time.

settings.title: The craft, in
settings.intro: From a single board of oak to a piece your grandchildren will argue over — this is how a Hearth & Grain piece comes to be.

features.title: Choose the timber
features.text: Every piece starts with a conversation about wood. We buy whole oak and walnut logs, mill them ourselves, and match each board to the life a piece will live — never to a catalog photo.

features.title: Draw it by hand
features.text: We sketch at full scale on the shop wall before any saw turns. Proportions get settled in pencil, in daylight, where a line that's wrong shows itself immediately.

features.title: Cut with patience
features.text: We rough-cut and then let the timber rest for weeks before final milling, so the wood settles into itself before we commit to the shape. Warp is our enemy; time is our tool.
features.detail: Timber is seasoned to the shop

features.title: Join by hand
features.text: Mortise and tenon, dovetail, and sliding joints — joined with hide glue and clamped until the wood forgets it was ever two pieces. We don't use a single screw where a joint will do.

features.title: Finish for the touch
features.text: We hand-rub three coats of hardwax oil into every surface until the oak takes on a depth you can feel before you see it. Brass hardware is waxed and lightly tarnished to match.

features.title: Guarantee it for life
features.text: Every joint and finish carries our lifetime guarantee. If a piece ever fails to be what we promised, we repair it free — or build you a new one. No fine print.

settings.title: From first talk
settings.intro: Whether it's a signature design or a fully bespoke commission, the path is the same — deliberate, transparent, and on time.

steps.title: Talk
steps.text: We sit down over the wood you're drawn to and talk about how you actually live with furniture — what you'll set on it, who'll use it, where it will sit in the light.

steps.title: Propose
steps.text: Within two weeks you get full-scale drawings, a real sample of the finish, and a fixed price. No estimates that balloon later.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Your piece is built by one maker from start to finish, over six to twelve weeks. We send progress photos at every stage, and you're welcome in the shop any Friday.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.text: We deliver, place, and level your piece ourselves — and set the brass hardware with you. Most deliveries end with us sitting on it together, checking the light.

steps.title: Live
steps.text: Furniture should settle in and improve with use. If anything ever needs care, our lifetime guarantee means we're a phone call away, always.

settings.note: Most of our work is now a referral — a client who bought one chair in 2004 and has furnished three homes with us since.

settings.title: Passed down,
settings.intro: The highest praise we get is a piece being fought over when someone moves house. A few of those stories.

reviews.quote: We bought the Founders Table in 2012. It's been through three moves, two kids doing homework at it, and a thousand dinners — and it looks better now than the day it arrived. My daughter has already called dibs.
reviews.author: Helen Parrish

reviews.quote: Hearth & Grain restored my grandmother's oak dining table with a cracked top. They matched the timber so well you can't find the repair in daylight. That table holds four generations of our family's Sunday dinners now.
reviews.author: Marcus Feld

reviews.quote: I'm a maker myself, so I'm hard to impress. Their joinery is genuinely flawless — mortise and tenon, hide glue, no screws. The Hearth Chair is the most comfortable thing I own and I expect it to outlive me.
reviews.author: Anita Rao

settings.title: Come sit
settings.intro: Our shop and showroom are open Friday to Monday. Coffee's always on, and you're welcome to sit on every piece — that's the only way to judge a chair.
